source_text:
Λευκίππης δὲ σωφρονέστατος βίος ἅπαντας ἐξίστησι, πῶς τετυμμένη κεκαρμένη τε
καὶ κατηχρειωμένη, τὸ δὴ μέγιστον, τρὶς θανοῦσ' ἐκαρτέρει.
orientation: The author is praising Leucippe, the female protagonist of the novel, whose supremely chaste life astonishes everyone through her endurance of suffering.
pass_a_gloss: And Leucippe's most chaste life amazes everyone: how, beaten and shorn and abused, and—the greatest thing indeed—having died three times, she endured.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'chaste' for σώφρων and 'life' for βίος; superlative rendered as 'most chaste'.
The verb means to drive out of one's senses, hence to astonish or amaze; 'amazes' captures the strong effect on everyone.
The perfect participle of καταχράομαι means 'misused' or 'abused'; 'abused' is the plainest literal rendering.

choices.english: having died three times, she endured
choices.why: The aorist participle θανοῦσα is concessive or circumstantial; the imperfect ἐκαρτέρει marks continued endurance. The clause order is kept.
rejected: though she died three times, she kept enduring

choices.why: The neuter article with δή marks a parenthetical superlative emphasis; 'indeed' preserves the particle's force.

pass_b_english: Leucippe's most chaste life amazes everyone: beaten, shorn, abused, and—greatest of all—having died three times, she endured.
